rows.source: HSE dairy-processing safety
rows.verified: Heavy loads and sharp-edged items make manual handling a main injury cause in dairy processing.

rows.source: HSE dairy-processing safety
rows.verified: Wet floors are a principal source of slips in dairy workplaces.

rows.source: HSE dairy-processing safety
rows.verified: Falling objects and hand tools are listed among struck-by hazards in dairy operations.

rows.source: HSE dairy-processing safety
rows.verified: Cleaning fluids, fumes, splashes, clean-in-place failures, steam and hot water can expose dairy workers to harmful substances and thermal hazards.

rows.source: HSE dairy-processing safety
rows.verified: Falls can occur from ladders, stairs, tanks, vehicles and tankers.

rows.source: HSE dairy-processing safety
rows.verified: Tanker movements and lift trucks are identified workplace-transport hazards in dairy processing.

rows.source: HSE dairy-processing safety
rows.verified: Lifting equipment, conveyors and packaging machines are among the machinery hazards listed for the dairy sector.

rows.source: HSE dairy-processing safety
rows.verified: Respiratory irritation can result from chlorine, hypochlorite or ammonia fumes generated by cleaning and refrigeration operations.

rows.source: HSE dairy-processing safety
rows.verified: Dairy risk depends on product line, wetness, cleaning chemistry, refrigeration, machinery, tanker traffic, temperature and work organisation.

rows.source: HSE dairy-processing safety
rows.verified: Dairy evidence is process-, chemical-, machine-, transport- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury or respiratory-risk probability.

rows.source: HSE alcoholic and soft-drink manufacturing safety
rows.verified: Barrels, casks and crates create substantial manual-handling risk in drink manufacturing.

rows.source: HSE alcoholic and soft-drink manufacturing safety
rows.verified: HSE reports that drink-sector slip injuries are strongly associated with wet floors, while trip hazards form the remaining share of slip-and-trip cases.

rows.source: HSE alcoholic and soft-drink manufacturing safety
rows.verified: Falling barrels, boxes and equipment can strike workers.

rows.source: HSE alcoholic and soft-drink manufacturing safety
rows.verified: Falls from ladders, work platforms, stairs and vehicles are identified sector hazards.

rows.source: HSE alcoholic and soft-drink manufacturing safety
rows.verified: Conveyors, bottling machines, packaging machines and palletisers are common machinery hazards in beverage plants.

rows.source: HSE alcoholic and soft-drink manufacturing safety
rows.verified: Cleaning chemicals, hot liquids and lift-truck movements create chemical, thermal and transport risks.

rows.source: HSE alcoholic and soft-drink manufacturing safety
rows.verified: Casking, kegging, decrating, washing, bottling, canning and packaging plant can create hazardous noise exposure.

rows.source: HSE alcoholic and soft-drink manufacturing safety
rows.verified: Grain and malt dust can cause occupational lung disease, while hardwood dust in cooperage work is associated with lung disease and nasal cancer risk.

rows.source: HSE alcoholic and soft-drink manufacturing safety
rows.verified: Drink-manufacturing risk depends on beverage process, container type, wetness, machinery, dust, noise, cleaning chemistry and material handling.

rows.source: HSE alcoholic and soft-drink manufacturing safety
rows.verified: Drink-industry evidence is process-, container-, machine-, exposure- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury or lung-disease probability.
